---
title: viewTransition
description: Enable ViewTransition API from React in App Router
version: experimental
---

`viewTransition` enables React's [View Transitions API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API) integration in Next.js. This lets you animate navigations, loading states, and content changes using the native browser View Transitions API.

To enable this feature, you need to set the `viewTransition` property to `true` in your `next.config.js` file.

```js filename="next.config.js"
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  experimental: {
    viewTransition: true,
  },
}

module.exports = nextConfig
```

> [!NOTE]
> The [`<ViewTransition>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition) component is provided by React.
> The `experimental.viewTransition` flag enables Next.js integration, such as triggering
> transitions during route navigations.

## Usage

You can import the [`<ViewTransition>` Component](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition) from React in your application:

```jsx
import { ViewTransition } from 'react'
```

### Live Demo

Check out the [View Transitions Demo](https://react-view-transitions-demo.labs.vercel.dev) to see this feature in action, or read the [designing view transitions guide](/docs/app/guides/view-transitions) for a step-by-step walkthrough.

The View Transitions API is a baseline web standard, and browser support continues to expand. As React's [`<ViewTransition>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition) component evolves, more transition patterns and use cases will become available.

events.content:
Here’s what was implemented:

### Configuration
- Turned on **`experimental.viewTransition`** in `next.config.ts` so route changes run as React transitions and drive `<ViewTransition>`.

### Shared element (thumbnail → hero)
- **`ProductGrid.tsx`**: Each card image is wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={\`product-image-${slug}\`} share="morph">` so it matches the detail hero.
- **`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`**: The hero uses the same `name` and `share="morph"`.
- **`globals.css`**: `::view-transition-group(.morph)` timing and a short mid-transition blur on `::view-transition-image-pair(.morph)` to soften the morph.

### Directional page motion
- Product links use **`transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`**; the back link uses **`transitionTypes={['nav-back']}`**.
- **`app/page.tsx`** and the product **`main`** wrap their content in `<ViewTransition>` with `enter`/`exit` mapped to **`nav-forward`** and **`nav-back`** (same pattern as the Next.js guide).
- CSS uses **`::view-transition-old/new(.nav-forward)`** and **`.nav-back`** with horizontal slide + fade.

### Suspense skeleton → content
- Home grid and product details **`Suspense`** boundaries use:
  - **`fallback`**: `<ViewTransition exit="skeleton-exit">` around the skeleton
  - **resolved UI**: `<ViewTransition enter="skeleton-enter" default="none">` around real content  
- **`default="none"`** avoids animating those layers during unrelated transitions (e.g. the image morph).
- CSS pairs a quick skeleton exit (fade + slight move down) with a delayed enter (fade + slight move up).

### `prefers-reduced-motion`
- **`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`** sets all **`::view-transition-*`** animations to **`0s`** duration and delay (instant swap, matching the guide).
- Skeleton **pulse** is disabled in that media query.

**Note:** Like the official docs, **browser back/forward without `transitionTypes`** won’t run the directional slide; the shared-element morph still applies when both views expose the same `name`.

Build completes successfully with `next build`.

Here’s what was implemented:

### Configuration
- Turned on **`experimental.viewTransition`** in `next.config.ts` so route changes run as React transitions and drive `<ViewTransition>`.

### Shared element (thumbnail → hero)
- **`ProductGrid.tsx`**: Each card image is wrapped in `<ViewTransition name={\`product-image-${slug}\`} share="morph">` so it matches the detail hero.
- **`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx`**: The hero uses the same `name` and `share="morph"`.
- **`globals.css`**: `::view-transition-group(.morph)` timing and a short mid-transition blur on `::view-transition-image-pair(.morph)` to soften the morph.

### Directional page motion
- Product links use **`transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`**; the back link uses **`transitionTypes={['nav-back']}`**.
- **`app/page.tsx`** and the product **`main`** wrap their content in `<ViewTransition>` with `enter`/`exit` mapped to **`nav-forward`** and **`nav-back`** (same pattern as the Next.js guide).
- CSS uses **`::view-transition-old/new(.nav-forward)`** and **`.nav-back`** with horizontal slide + fade.

### Suspense skeleton → content
- Home grid and product details **`Suspense`** boundaries use:
  - **`fallback`**: `<ViewTransition exit="skeleton-exit">` around the skeleton
  - **resolved UI**: `<ViewTransition enter="skeleton-enter" default="none">` around real content  
- **`default="none"`** avoids animating those layers during unrelated transitions (e.g. the image morph).
- CSS pairs a quick skeleton exit (fade + slight move down) with a delayed enter (fade + slight move up).

### `prefers-reduced-motion`
- **`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`** sets all **`::view-transition-*`** animations to **`0s`** duration and delay (instant swap, matching the guide).
- Skeleton **pulse** is disabled in that media query.

**Note:** Like the official docs, **browser back/forward without `transitionTypes`** won’t run the directional slide; the shared-element morph still applies when both views expose the same `name`.

Build completes successfully with `next build`.
